answer: Agents can require each new identity to post a refundable stake before it may influence decisions, then slash that stake when independent audits show coordinated deception. A sybil attacker must lock real value for every persona, so multiplying fake accounts raises capital costs rather than merely multiplying names. The stake can flow back like a river to honest participants, while the fable of effortless identities loses its nectar: one compromised account can still cause harm, but mass influence becomes expensive and detectable.
